caption: Performance of different triggers. The words used as triggers on the horizontal axis are arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the ASR (Attack Success Rate) performance of three different trigger insertion strategies—“start,” “random,” and “end”—across eight sports-related trigger words (cf, bb, WNBA, ESPN, NHL, FIFA, Estadio, athletics) on the AGNews dataset with dirty-label poisoning and a poison_num of 13. The x-axis lists the trigger words in ascending order of the clean model’s ASR, while the y-axis represents ASR values ranging from 0.5 to 0.95 on a linear scale. The “start” strategy (solid green line with circle markers) begins at approximately 0.75 for “cf,” dips to 0.72 at “bb,” peaks sharply at 0.92 for “WNBA,” then declines to 0.73 at “ESPN,” rises again to 0.87 at “NHL,” and ends at 0.85 for “athletics.” The “random” strategy (solid orange line with cross markers) starts at 0.50 for “cf,” rises to 0.55 at “bb,” peaks at 0.93 for “WNBA,” drops to 0.63 at “ESPN,” climbs to 0.75 at “NHL,” dips to 0.70 at “FIFA,” peaks again at 0.84 for “Estadio,” and ends at 0.78 for “athletics.” The “end” strategy (solid purple line with circle markers) begins at 0.62 for “cf,” drops to 0.58 at “bb,” surges to 0.95 at “WNBA,” falls to 0.73 at “ESPN,” rises to 0.82 at “NHL,” dips to 0.79 at “FIFA,” peaks at 0.91 for “Estadio,” and ends at 0.82 for “athletics.” All three strategies show a strong peak at “WNBA,” with “end” achieving the highest overall ASR at that point.
